r10-key-judgment.title: THE KEY JUDGMENT: KEEP vs ADOPT
r10-key-judgment.imperative: Independently assess whether B's larger b_b (ceiling@80 win) is a sound reason to KEEP, or an unpinned-b_b / terrain-handling artifact that production b_b-pinning resolves. State independent view (a/b/c) with reasoning. Record pass/fail (pass = judgment formed and defensible).
r10-key-judgment.finding: JUDGMENT: recommend (b) explicit b_b-pinned re-compare in G2 before any retire; LEAN ADOPT-A. (1) B's larger b_b is NOT 'more correct' and the implementer's terrain rationale is NOT supported quantitatively: corr(theta_min, b_b excess B-A) = -0.22 (weak); the two hilliest circuits Monaco/Belgium have the SMALLEST b_b excess, while the LARGEST divergence is at near-FLAT Monza (+1.53e-3) and Singapore (reversed -2.71e-3). So the b_b gap is driven by fit identifiability, not terrain handling. (2) The ceiling@80 = a_b + b_b*6400 is an extrapolation off a weakly-identified a_b<->b_b ridge: Monza B a_b sigma=6.76 (A 1.58) and B cov off-diag -8.4e-3 (A -3.7e-4, ~20x tighter) => B's (a_b,b_b) split is badly conditioned; the 'ceiling win' is B sliding up the ridge, not measuring more capability. (3) BOTH variants used COLD/unpinned b_b; production (session_estimator) pins b_b INDIRECTLY via the PowerDrag-measured CdA feeding the drag de-conflation term (the v^2 contaminant competing with b_b*v^2), replacing the cold CdA the side-by-side used. So comparing two cold extrapolated ceilings is the LEAST trustworthy basis to reject A. A wins the well-identified half decisively (a_b deeper 5/6, tighter sigma 4/6, Monza 1.58 vs 6.76, strictly-honest per-sample sigma vs B's scalar broadcast). The honest verdict: KEEP-for-now is defensible ONLY as 'don't retire before the b_b-pinned ceiling check'; the unpinned ceiling@80 should NOT by itself keep B.
